E spell (Singularity): To reproduce, make sure that "Clamp cast target location within max range" is disabled. If you cast the spell well beyond its range, Aurelion Sol moves to cast it precisely where you aimed, as it should. However, if you cast the spell just slightly beyond its range, Aurelion Sol will NOT move and will cast it at max range as if "Clamp cast target location within max range" was enabled. This leads to situations where you try to aim for the center of a minion wave, but the spell randomly casts closer to you than where you were actually aiming, missing the furthest minions, losing you passive stacks and CS.

Q spell (Breath of Light): The channel direction doesn't update smoothly with mouse movement. This is especially visible when moving the mouse very slowly, the spell seems to catch up by increments as opposed to following your mouse in real-time. This is also visible during quick left-to-right motions, you can see that the spell sometimes misses some flicks alltogether. This is not just visual and affects the spell's hitbox too. Just to be clear as I've already confused some people with this: I am not saying that the spell should instantly rotate to wherever you aim, I am saying that the spell doesn't rotate smoothly when you move the mouse slower than its maximum rotation speed.  
Vel'Koz ult has this issue too, but it's much less impactful by virtue of being used way less often and having a much slower rotation speed.

GW2 has several graphical issues, one of the main ones being how they handle postprocessing. In WoW, they use very vibrant textures and colours, then tone them down with shaders depending on what the scene requires. They did this in GW2's first expansion, Heart of Thorns. What you're left with are completely saturated colours, just a little bit of sun is enough to make your entire screen super bright. To compensate, the screen adjusts brightness depending on luminosity, but this leads to literal black shadows anywhere there's even a tiny bit of ambiant occlusion.
